plan.summary: Report indicates a Samsung Galaxy A53 5G powers on and displays an image, but touch input is unresponsive, with unverified claims of prior liquid exposure.

hypotheses.mechanism: Digitizer assembly failure or damage to display flexible printed circuit (FPC)
hypotheses.why: The screen powers on and renders graphics normally, but swipe gestures and touch input fail entirely across the panel.
hypotheses.safe_test: Inspect the display surface externally under magnification for hairline cracks or physical deformation without opening the enclosure.

hypotheses.mechanism: Corrosion or pin bridging at the display/digitizer connector or motherboard touch circuitry due to liquid ingress
hypotheses.why: Unverified testimony mentions past water damage, which frequently corrodes connector contacts or causes intermittent shorts in touch power/data lines.
hypotheses.safe_test: Inspect exterior seams, USB-C port, and the SIM card tray opening with an external light source for moisture indicator discoloration or corrosion residue without disassembling or powering with external mains.

hypotheses.mechanism: Temporary OS-level touch input processing freeze or unresponsive touch driver
hypotheses.why: Device powered on after being unused since a past date and may be stalled at lockscreen driver initialization.
hypotheses.safe_test: Perform a non-invasive hardware key forced restart (holding Power/Side + Volume Down buttons) while disconnected from chargers to observe if touch recovers without wiping user data.

plan.next_safe_check: Perform a visual external inspection of the frame, glass, and ports, followed by a non-invasive forced restart using external physical buttons while observing lithium-ion battery safety precautions.
plan.uncertainty: All liquid damage assertions originate from unverified conversational speech rather than objective inspection, and internal board/connector states remain unobserved.
